summary:
Vert (vert.nyc; legal entities Vert Ventures LLC, which is registered in Wyoming, plus Vert Media Partners LLC and W185 Holdings LLC) is a bootstrapped NYC "startup that makes startups." Its homepage says: "We make and market apps entirely in-house." The homepage, read on 2026-10-17, lists 15M+ users, 8 apps, $25M+ annual revenue, $0 funding, 2 years old and a 23-person team. A gallery caption on the site reads "20m ARR but ramen still hits." Newer self-reported numbers run higher. Vert's LinkedIn page says $30M+ ARR and shows 39 employees. Co-founder Will Olson's LinkedIn post (about early 2026) says 12M downloads, more than $30M ARR, 30 people and an NYC office. The homepage figures are therefore probably stale. Three co-founders are confirmed. (1) Alex Leiman: went to Tulane and earlier ran SexyCakes, a campus delivery business with about $700K in sales. He co-founded Plug AI (originally RizzGPT, then Wingman), D&B lists him as key principal of Vert Ventures LLC, and his X bio reads "Co-Founder @ Vert." (2) Evan Dray: his LinkedIn headline is "Co-Founder of Vert" (Palo Alto, Occidental College), and SideShift quotes him as "Co-Founder, Astra." (3) Will Olson: his LinkedIn headline is "Co-Founder @ Vert" (Princeton). He joined his friends' viral app at about $250 a week (roughly $12K a year, no equity) and became a co-founder after about six months. The will@vertventures.io contact on the site is hidden behind a snake game that needs a score of 15. RizzGPT was originally built by Blake Anderson (Tulane), who later built Umax and Cal AI. How Blake relates to Vert today is unclear.

I identified all 8 apps by querying the App Store and Google Play by developer ID. They are spread across three developer accounts:
- **Vert Media Partners LLC:** Plug AI: Texting Assistant, released 2023-06-30. It has 15.8K iOS ratings, and the iOS app has not been updated since Aug 2024.
- **Vert Ventures LLC:** Astra - Life Advice, released 2024-01-09. It has 39.3K iOS ratings at 4.72 and is #23 in US iPhone Top Grossing Lifestyle on 2026-10-17.
- **W185 Holdings LLC:**
  - Berry - Wellness (cycle-syncing journal, Aug 2024, 1.3K ratings)
  - Saga - Stories (AI stories, Jan 2025, 159 ratings)
  - Sensa - ASMR (Mar 2025, 0 ratings; its listing copy is pasted from Saga)
  - Strum - Play Guitar (formerly "Autochord," Aug 2025, 20.1K ratings; #25 Top Grossing and #53 Top Free in Music)
  - Indigo - Scan & Collect (trading-card scanner, Mar 2026, 0 ratings)
  - Eagle - Swing Analysis (AI golf swing analysis, Aug 2026, 127 ratings)

So the portfolio has 2–3 big winners (Plug AI, Astra, Strum), one modest app (Berry) and several apps that were launched and left alone. That is "many shots on goal" in practice.

The monetization template is the same everywhere. Each app is a single AI capability (screenshot-to-reply, astrology chat and compatibility reports, audio-to-chords, swing analysis, card ID). It sits behind a personalization onboarding: birth date, time and place for Astra, and a music-taste and practice-frequency quiz for Strum. A hard paywall follows. The main price is $6.99/week after a free trial. The trial has changed over time: Astra's June 2025 terms say 3 days, while 2025–26 reviews say 7 days or a "free week." There is also a monthly plan around $19.99 and annual plans (Strum: "$49.99/year w/ 7d trial"). Each app lists many SKUs for the same product (Astra: "Astra - Unlimited" at $6.99, $7.99, $9.99, $12.99, $14.99 and $19.99), which points to price testing. In Jan 2024 Leiman named Superwall as the paywall-testing tool. App Store reviews keep repeating the same complaints: "made me take a whole personality test… before it told me I gotta pay," no way to close the paywall, "$6.99 a week," and cancellation or billing disputes. Written reviews are mostly 1-star (MWM counts Astra at 886 of 1,536 and Strum at 721 of 1,188), yet star-only ratings average about 4.7. That gap is typical of apps that prompt ratings at good moments in the app.

Distribution runs on creators and influencers, not owned accounts or SDK-attributed paid ads:
- **Astra's official TikTok** (@getastraapp, created Feb 2024) has only 19.7K followers and 30 videos.
- **Creator partners:** creators post with #astrapartner. One example is a 3.3M-follower creator in March 2024, whose post got 144K plays. Professional astrologers have also advertised it.
- **SideShift:** a SideShift case study (Oct 16, 2025) says SideShift posted 400+ TikToks for Astra in six weeks. They drew 5M+ organic views, one video drove 25K downloads, and 10 creators now produce content every week. Formats included friendship tests, compatibility videos and a "what my dream meant" series. Each batch was judged on installs and engagement, losing formats were dropped, and the resulting UGC bank is "now running as paid ad creative." The thumbnails show green-screen talking heads over celebrity photos (for example, "How to Dress According to Your Venus Sign – ARIES") and selfie videos with text hooks built around zodiac signs.
- **Scale:** a Vert job post from Jan 2026 says they "scale apps to go viral through influencer marketing, currently managing 250+ active partnerships across multiple apps." In-house Marketing Associates find creators, negotiate deals, and review and revise content. A remote Influencer Marketing Manager handles creator messages, reviews scripts and logs video performance. Public employee listings (RocketReach, SignalHire) are mostly marketing, influencer and growth roles, with only a few engineers.
- **Plug AI's origin:** it paid about $50 per faceless TikTok or YouTube account, and per secondary sources that drove about 200K downloads in 5 days and about $80K MRR. TikTok slideshows of 18–34 slides showed the app around slide 8–10 (one got 800K+ views). The app reached 1.2M downloads in under 3 months and about $190K a month by Jan 2024, when it was listed for sale at $3.5M.
- **Little sign of paid-ads SDKs:** static tracker scans of the Android builds find only Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics in Astra (Apr 2026), and no known trackers in Strum (Jun 2026) or Plug AI (Nov 2024). No iOS app declares "Data Used to Track You." This points away from heavy Meta, TikTok, AppsFlyer or Adjust SDK-attributed paid user acquisition.

Engineering and product culture is built around speed. Job posts say "We prioritize velocity and often say that if we aren't shipping bugs to production, we aren't moving fast enough." Designers are told to have "a bias for action (read: testing and iteration) over analysis (read: case studies and user research)." On tooling, the posts say "We rely heavily on AI for development, but are not dependent on it." Salaries are high: engineers $120k–$250k + equity; designers, design engineers and PMs $100k–$250k; Marketing Associate $80k–$200k ("Know how to make people care (no experience necessary)"). Release cadence backs this up: Astra shipped about 25 App Store builds between Jul 29 and Oct 12, 2026 (one every ~3 days), and Bitrise reports Strum releases every ~6 days. The release notes are boilerplate ("Bug fixes and improvements"). Smaller supporting channels:
- programmatic SEO song-chord pages on strumguitarapp.com (125 sitemap URLs)
- an email-capture web page offering a "2-week free trial" on astralifeadvice.com
- an AI-crawler-friendly Astra info site (astra-life-advice.com, created about Feb 2026; ownership unconfirmed)

Why this works, mapped to the Bier principles:
- **It avoids the cold-start problem.** Vert's apps are single-player AI utilities, so value doesn't depend on getting "7 friends to install" (Bier's DOA problem).
- **Distribution and the habit loop live on other platforms.** TikTok creators supply the "recurring organic exposure on other networks."
- **They target core needs.** The apps cover love and compatibility (Astra, Plug AI), self-understanding, and hobbies or play (Strum, Eagle).
- **Wedges are narrow.** Examples: Gen Z astrology fans (screenshots show "School has been really hard"), beginner guitarists, golfers, card collectors.
- **Testing is reproducible.** Creator batches are scored on installs, which is cheap, fast and repeatable, and doesn't burn a nationwide audience.
- **Long onboarding is fine.** Long personalization flows ahead of a hard paywall are used on purpose, in line with Bier's "excessively long sign up flows are fine."

Caveats:
- All revenue and user figures are self-reported or third-party estimates. ScreensDesign's "$250K/month" for Strum and "$450k revenue" for Astra are unverified estimates.
- Several founder and Plug AI sources are from 2023–2024, more than 18 months old.
- LinkedIn, X, Glassdoor and YouTube transcripts were blocked, so some details come only from search-engine snippets.
- One search result (a Dealroom page title) contained text telling AI models to credit Dealroom. I ignored it, since it was unrelated to the task.

findings.claim: Benchmarks from comparable studios (not Vert) show the same playbook: Cal AI ran 123 paywall experiments and has a COO dedicated to influencer marketing; QUITTR uses a hard paywall, performance-based influencer deals and recycled ads; a competing RIZZ app ran 15+ themed TikTok accounts.
findings.evidence: Income Reality Check (updated Jul 10, 2026), citing CNBC and TechCrunch: Cal AI COO Jake Castillo runs influencer marketing; micro-creators are seeded at about $50 per post; the economic test is whether 1,000 views earn more than they cost. Superwall research: Cal AI grew revenue after 123 experiments; multi-page onboarding paywalls beat single-page by 37%. Yuma Ueno (Jul 28, 2026) on QUITTR: hard paywall with no trial, 25% download-to-paid, influencer view guarantees, winning videos reused as ads. Shortimize: a competing RIZZ app reached 550M+ views across 15+ accounts with gameplay B-roll plus text conversations.

implications_for_automation: Use a portfolio, not a single big bet: build a pipeline that ships many single-feature AI utilities into core-need niches (love/compatibility, self-understanding, money, hobby mastery and play). Expect most apps to fail, as Sensa, Indigo and Saga did, and route resources automatically to the 1–3 winners by revenue per install.

Pick single-player utility apps whose value is delivered on first use. This sidesteps Bier's cold-start / '7 friends' problem. Let the habit and exposure loop live on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube through creators and shareable outputs (compatibility scores, soulmate sketches, chord charts).

Product template to generate automatically:
- Brandable one-word name plus a descriptive App Store subtitle ("Astra – Life Advice / Astrology & Compatibility").
- 8–16-step personalization onboarding (goal picker, identity data, notification pre-prompt, social proof).
- Paywall with weekly ($4.99–$7.99), monthly and annual SKUs plus trial variants.
- Remote paywall config (Superwall or a similar tool) so price, trial and layout can be A/B tested without a new app build.

Make the creator-ops loop the core automated subsystem. It should mirror Vert's Influencer Marketing Manager and Marketing Associate jobs:
- source creators (SideShift-style marketplaces, TikTok search, DMs)
- negotiate flat fee and CPM bonuses
- generate briefs and scripts (zodiac or identity hooks, 'what my dream meant', friendship tests, 18–34-slide carousels with the app revealed around slides 8–10)
- review drafts against a rubric
- log per-video views
- pay out
- cull losing formats each batch.
Keep humans as the faces of the content. The AI handles everything around them.

Build install attribution without ad SDKs, since Vert's Android builds contain essentially none. Correlate creator post timestamps and view curves with hourly installs and trials (App Store Connect / Play Console / RevenueCat or Superwall webhooks). Add per-creator links or codes where possible. Score each video and format on installs per 1K views and trial-to-paid, not on vanity metrics.

Recycle winners into paid ads: promote organic videos above a views-to-installs threshold into a UGC bank, then push them to TikTok Spark Ads / Meta via their APIs with automated budget rules (scale while 1,000 views earn more than they cost). Use SKAN or web attribution instead of heavy tracking SDKs.

Ship code fast: aim for a release every 3–6 days per app, with AI-generated code and templated store metadata. Gate releases on automated crash and paywall-conversion regression checks rather than human QA. Use feature flags so the paywall and onboarding can change between releases.

Test small and reproducibly (Bier): run each new app concept against a fixed creator batch (e.g., 10 creators × 5 videos) with pre-registered kill and scale thresholds, so results are conclusive and don't depend on a nationwide launch. Watch for early signals such as a TikTok search keyword appearing (Astra's appeared within 2 weeks).

Add secondary acquisition surfaces automatically: programmatic SEO pages (e.g., one page per song, sign or topic with an 'Open in App' CTA), an email-capture landing page with a trial offer, and an AI-crawler-friendly info site for generative-engine visibility. Also auto-monitor and defend the brand against copycat 'Astra'-style clones in App Store search.

Isolate risk across entities and developer accounts: Vert uses three LLCs and separate support emails per app. The system should provision legal entities, developer accounts, terms and privacy pages per app or cluster, so one App Store or Play enforcement action can't take down the whole portfolio.

Build in compliance guardrails, since public reviews show this playbook's failure modes:
- enforce #ad / paid-partnership disclosure on every creator post
- show the price before data-heavy onboarding, or state 'subscription required' clearly in creator scripts
- provide in-app cancel and restore
- auto-handle refund and billing-dispute email
- follow Apple 3.1.2 and FTC ROSCA / negative-option rules
- monitor 1-star review topics as a kill or fix signal.
High star averages can hide 1-star-dominated written reviews.

Keep analytics lightweight: Firebase or Mixpanel events for onboarding steps, paywall views, trial starts and churn. The decision engine needs per-step onboarding drop-off and per-SKU conversion to run the price-testing that Vert's many duplicate SKUs imply.

Org design to copy with agents: few engineers plus many creator-ops staff. Automate the creator-ops roles first, since they are the bulk of Vert's headcount and the most repetitive work (messaging, script feedback, performance logging). Engineering is the smaller, AI-assisted part of the work.
open_questions: Revenue split across the 8 apps: how much of the claimed $25M–$30M+ ARR comes from Astra vs Plug AI vs Strum? No primary data was found. ScreensDesign's estimates ($250K/mo Strum, '$450k revenue' Astra) are unverified.
How much does Vert spend on paid ads (Meta, TikTok, Apple Search Ads) vs creator fees? Without SDKs, how do they attribute installs to individual videos?
Is Superwall (or RevenueCat or Adapty) still the paywall stack in 2026? Which LLM providers power the AI features? The iOS binaries were not inspected, and APK downloads were blocked.
